A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.9. Retained content can be reliably aligned despite pagination changes and added experiments.

before.justification: V4 reports original CQL and IQL experiments on five Procgen games, including returns and optimal mixing weights in Figures 2–4 and Tables 1–4.

after.justification: V5 retains the original Procgen results and adds IQL experiments on HalfCheetah and HumanoidStandup in Figures 5–7.

M1.justification: The weighted target/source TD-error objective in Equation (10), Bellman updates, and mixing-weight formulation are unchanged. The MuJoCo experiments reuse IQL without introducing a new method component or weight-learning procedure.

E1.justification: Section 4.2 adds HalfCheetah and HumanoidStandup with source/target gravity and friction mismatches. This substantially broadens coverage from five procedural game environments to continuous-control tasks with explicit physical dynamics changes.

E2.justification: Procgen retains CQL and IQL with the same mixing-weight comparisons. MuJoCo uses the existing IQL backbone. Revisions to the H2O and ORIS discussion do not add or remove an actually evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The added MuJoCo protocols use source sizes of 80,000 and 100,000, with target-size grids of {3,000, 5,000, 8,000} and {6,000, 8,000, 10,000}, respectively. They retain the seven-weight sweep; existing Procgen splits, sample sizes, and Table 5 settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 6–7 add MuJoCo sensitivity studies of optimal mixing weight versus physics mismatch and target sample count. These extend the existing Procgen bias–variance investigations with controlled physical perturbations while retaining the same analysis questions.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their mean and standard-deviation summaries, and both versions display plot error bars. V5 adds no repeated-run counts, training-seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Procgen Figures 2–4 and Tables 1–4 are unchanged, but Figures 5–7 add a substantial set of MuJoCo returns and optimal-weight results. Both far-source comparisons in Figure 5 peak at the sampled weight 0.2; subsequent plots show optimal weights increasing with smaller mismatch and decreasing with more target data.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, performance bounds, closed-form optimal weight, convergence result, and proofs in Appendices A.1–A.7 are unchanged. Calling the MDP tabular makes the existing finite-state/action restriction explicit.

C1.justification: Section 1.2 qualifies the novelty claim as an algorithm-agnostic framework for balancing datasets prior to the actual learning process. The central claims about performance bounds, optimal weighting under simplifying assumptions, and convergence are retained.

C2.justification: V5 adds a qualification that larger datasets can still fail when samples leave coverage gaps, explains how Procgen layouts affect transitions, and explicitly describes the worst-case bound as primarily conceptual. The limitation concerning practical computation of optimal weights already appeared in v4.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 documents MuJoCo source construction using gravity/friction scale pairs (0.85, 0.85), (0.90, 0.90), and (0.95, 0.95), together with IQL use and dataset sizes. The Procgen hyperparameters in Appendix Table 5 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V5 replaces the fixed-weight characterizations and Equation (10) recovery claims for H2O/ORIS with a discussion of their sample-dependent weighting, distinguishing its own balancing before learning. It also adds Packer et al. (2018) and Kirk et al. (2023) on generalization.

P1.justification: Section 4 is reorganized into Procgen and MuJoCo subsections, with localized rewrites concerning prior work, scope, and interpretation. Author contact details, publication information, and acknowledgments are added; most method and theory prose and the proof structure are retained.

P2.justification: V5 adds MuJoCo Figures 5–7 and the two-level Maze illustration in Appendix Figure 13. Existing screenshots are retained as Figures 8–12. The title page and headers change, and Tables 3–4 move, while retained plots and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The MuJoCo experiments strengthen empirical support for the existing qualitative trade-off predictions through explicitly controlled physical changes beyond Procgen. Revised prior-work positioning and the coverage qualification improve precision. These are meaningful but limited gains to a paper whose central mathematical contribution and original results remain unchanged.
